What worked: install a trap in the page (MutationObserver on <video> plus hooks on fetch and XHR) that writes the first media URL it sees into sessionStorage, which SURVIVES the navigation Flow does when you open a clip; then open the clip editor, press play, let the page fetch its own video as a Blob, and PUT that Blob straight to a Higgsfield presigned URL; then curl it down on the Mac. Two traps: no <video> element exists until the clip editor is open and playing, and the presigned URL's embedded STS token expires much sooner than its own X-Amz-Expires claims, so mint it immediately before the PUT. The first attempt failed 400 ExpiredToken, which was only visible because the response body was read instead of the status code being guessed.", "SETTLED, and it is the best seam result on the free route: same still in both frame slots gives 2.774 and 2.559 with no accumulation across clips. Flow delivers a ZIP, not an mp4, and every clip's file is named from the first words of the prompt, so three identical prompts produce three identically named files. 1) Run palette_gate.py on the opening still BEFORE spending a single video credit. Canon lines do not see colour. 2) Evening or night only. Keep Coco curled, or put the structural face spec into the VIDEO prompt and not only the still prompt. 5) Never name an architectural feature that is not already in the still. The single word 'doorway' drew a wooden door into the room.
